evidence: This is supported by computational prediction shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citations to previous work.

claim: Intrinsically disordered domains are a feature shared by many proteins that undergo assembly into RNP particles.
source: Consistent with these findings, Sts5 contains a region predicted to be intrinsically disordered in the first 301 amino acids of the Sts5 protein, a feature shared by many proteins that undergo assembly into RNP particles (Lin et al., 2015; Patel et al., 2015; Elbaum-Garfinkle et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2014; Kato et al., 2012; Han et al., 2012) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Sts5 proteins can organize in cytoplasmic puncta during mitosis and in response to nutritional stress.
source: These results indicate that Sts5 proteins can organize in cytoplasmic puncta during mitosis and in response to nutritional stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data presented.

claim: Sts5 puncta co-localize with P-bodies following glucose or nitrogen starvation.
source: Furthermore, these puncta co-localize with P-bodies following glucose or nitrogen starvation.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Microarray analysis identified 140 mRNAs that are elevated at least 1.9-fold in sts5Δ mutants as compared to wild-type cells under exponential growth conditions.
source: To investigate the functions of Sts5-regulated transcripts, we first used microarray analysis to identify mRNAs that are elevated (at least 1.9-fold) in sts5Δ mutants as compared to wild-type cells, under exponential growth conditions (See Figure 3—source data 1). This analysis identified 140 mRNAs, and showed significant overrepresentation of genes with roles in polarized cell growth, adhesion and cell wall biogenesis by gene ontology enrichment analysis (Figure 3, *) (See Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data presented in Figure 3 and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Gene ontology enrichment analysis showed significant overrepresentation of genes with roles in polarized cell growth, adhesion and cell wall biogenesis among mRNAs elevated in sts5Δ mutants.
source: This analysis identified 140 mRNAs, and showed significant overrepresentation of genes with roles in polarized cell growth, adhesion and cell wall biogenesis by gene ontology enrichment analysis (Figure 3, *) (See Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Microarray analysis identified ssp1, cmk2, tea5/ppk2, ksg1 and lkh1, which encode protein kinases with a role in the activation of bipolar cell growth.
source: Remarkably, we identified ssp1, cmk2, tea5/ppk2, ksg1 and lkh1, which encode protein kinases with a role in the activation of bipolar cell growth (Figure 3; Figure 3—source data 1) (Koyano et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 3 and a citation to previous work.

claim: mRNAs encoding polarity regulators ssp1, cmk2, tea5/ppk2, ksg1 and lkh1 all contain a consensus sequence in their 5'UTR which functions as a potential recognition sequence for targets of the S. cerevisiae homolog of Sts5, Ssd1.
source: Intriguingly, these mRNAs encoding polarity regulators all contain a consensus sequence in their 5'UTR which functions as a potential recognition sequence for targets of the S. cerevisiae homolog of Sts5, Ssd1 (Figure 3, †) (Hogan et al., 2008) (Wanless et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis and citations to previous work.

claim: qPCR analysis confirmed that sts5Δ cells exhibit increased levels of ssp1, cmk2, tea5/ppk2, lkh1, efc25, and psu1 mRNA.
source: The mRNAs encoding proteins with known roles in polarized cell growth were selected for further analysis by qPCR, which confirmed that sts5Δ cells exhibit increased levels of ssp1, cmk2, tea5/ppk2, lkh1, efc25, and psu1 mRNA, genes with diverse functions in cell morphogenesis (Figure 4A) (Figure 3; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Sts5-3xGFP protein co-purifies with efc25, ssp1, and psu1 mRNAs.
source: Further, we determined that Sts5-3xGFP protein co-purifies with efc25, ssp1, and psu1 mRNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ssp1 was previously identified as an extragenic suppressor of sts5 mutants.
source: Consistent with a functional interaction with sts5 and orb6, ssp1 was previously identified as an extragenic suppressor of sts5 mutants (Matsusaka et al., 1995), while psu1 functions as a multicopy suppressor of orb6 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: psu1 functions as a multicopy suppressor of orb6 mutants.
source: Consistent with a functional interaction with sts5 and orb6, ssp1 was previously identified as an extragenic suppressor of sts5 mutants (Matsusaka et al., 1995), while psu1 functions as a multicopy suppressor of orb6 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ssp1 protein levels significantly increase in sts5∆ mutants, as compared to controls, when cells are exposed to higher temperatures (36°C).
source: We determined that Ssp1 protein levels significantly increase in sts5∆ mutants, as compared to controls, when cells are exposed to higher temperatures (36°C; Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: sts5∆ cells display a temperature-sensitive morphological phenotype, growing over a wider area of the cell surface and developing a rounded cell shape at 36°C.
source: Interestingly, sts5∆ cells display a temperature-sensitive morphological phenotype, growing over a wider area of the cell surface and developing a rounded cell shape at 36°C (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,d).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The aberrant morphological phenotype of sts5 mutants is partially suppressed by loss of ssp1.
source: Consistent with increased Ssp1 protein levels playing a role in promoting abnormal morphogenesis, the aberrant morphological phenotype of sts5 mutants is partially suppressed by loss of ssp1 (Matsusaka et al., 1995; Toda et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Loss of sts5 leads to increased levels of Myc-Efc25 proteins as compared to control sts5+ cells.
source: In addition, we determined that loss of sts5 leads also to increased levels of Myc-Efc25 proteins as compared to the control sts5+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and 2C.

claim: Sts5 has a role in regulating the cellular abundance of specific mRNAs, affecting cell morphology in particular during cell stress.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate a role for Sts5 in regulating the cellular abundance of specific mRNAs, affecting cell morphology in particular during cell stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Levels of Ssp1 protein are increased in both the pdc1∆ and edc3∆ mutant backgrounds.
source: We found that levels of Ssp1 protein are increased, as compared to tubulin control, in both the pdc1∆ and edc3∆ mutant backgrounds (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: P-body components modulate mRNA abundance even in the absence of large P-body formation.
source: This effect is seen even in the absence of starvation, during exponential cell growth, consistent with the idea that P-body components modulate mRNA abundance even in the absence of large P-body formation (Decker et al., 2007; Eulalio et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: ssp1 mRNA readily co-localizes to Sts5- and Dcp1-containing granules in cells re-diluted in minimal medium lacking glucose for 20 min.
source: We found that ssp1 mRNA readily co-localizes to Sts5- and Dcp1-containing granules in cells re-diluted in minimal medium (EMM) lacking glucose for 20 min (Figure 4G; Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: No co-localization of ssp1 mRNA with Sts5- and Dcp1-containing granules was observed in control cells re-diluted in growth medium containing 2% glucose.
source: Conversely, no co-localization was observed in control cells re-diluted in growth medium containing 2% glucose (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A-C).
evidence: This is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Sts5 and P-body components have a role in regulating the levels of ssp1 mRNA and Ssp1 protein.
source: Our data reveal a role for Sts5 and P-body components in regulating the levels of ssp1 mRNA and Ssp1 protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: In orb6-as2 cells treated with the 1-NA-PP1 inhibitor, Sts5-3xGFP rapidly coalesces into cytoplasmic puncta that colocalize with the P-body marker Dcp1-mCherry.
source: In orb6-as2 cells treated with the 1-NA-PP1 inhibitor, Sts5-3xGFP rapidly coalesces into cytoplasmic puncta that colocalize with the P-body marker Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, d, h, and l; see quantification in Figure 5B), while DMSO-treated cells exhibit diffuse cytoplasmic localization of Sts5-3xGFP and Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, c, g, and k and Figure 5B), supporting the idea that Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into RNP granules and Sts5 co-localization with P-bodies.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: DMSO-treated orb6-as2 cells exhibit diffuse cytoplasmic localization of Sts5-3xGFP and Dcp1-mCherry.
source: In orb6-as2 cells treated with the 1-NA-PP1 inhibitor, Sts5-3xGFP rapidly coalesces into cytoplasmic puncta that colocalize with the P-body marker Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, d, h, and l; see quantification in Figure 5B), while DMSO-treated cells exhibit diffuse cytoplasmic localization of Sts5-3xGFP and Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, c, g, and k and Figure 5B), supporting the idea that Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into RNP granules and Sts5 co-localization with P-bodies.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into RNP granules.
source: In orb6-as2 cells treated with the 1-NA-PP1 inhibitor, Sts5-3xGFP rapidly coalesces into cytoplasmic puncta that colocalize with the P-body marker Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, d, h, and l; see quantification in Figure 5B), while DMSO-treated cells exhibit diffuse cytoplasmic localization of Sts5-3xGFP and Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, c, g, and k and Figure 5B), supporting the idea that Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into RNP granules and Sts5 co-localization with P-bodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5 co-localization with P-bodies.
source: In orb6-as2 cells treated with the 1-NA-PP1 inhibitor, Sts5-3xGFP rapidly coalesces into cytoplasmic puncta that colocalize with the P-body marker Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, d, h, and l; see quantification in Figure 5B), while DMSO-treated cells exhibit diffuse cytoplasmic localization of Sts5-3xGFP and Dcp1-mCherry (Figure 5A, c, g, and k and Figure 5B), supporting the idea that Orb6 kinase negatively regulates Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into RNP granules and Sts5 co-localization with P-bodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The formation of RNP granules often occurs as a result of liquid-liquid phase transition controlled by the concentration of RNP component proteins.
source: Recent work has shown that the formation of RNP granules often occurs as a result of liquid-liquid phase transition controlled by the concentration of RNP component proteins (Kroschwald et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2015; Elbaum-Garfinkle et al., 2015; Patel et al., 2015; Kato et al., 2012; Hyman et al., 2014; Brangwynne et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2013; Brangwynne, 2013; Becker and Gitler, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The number of Dcp1-mCherry granules was significantly reduced in the sts5∆ background following Orb6-as2 kinase inhibition.
source: Interestingly, we found that the number of Dcp1-mCherry granules was significantly reduced in the sts5∆ background, indicating that Sts5 recruitment has a role in promoting P-body formation (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Sts5 recruitment has a role in promoting P-body formation.
source: Interestingly, we found that the number of Dcp1-mCherry granules was significantly reduced in the sts5∆ background, indicating that Sts5 recruitment has a role in promoting P-body formation (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Orb6 kinase can induce P-body formation via Sts5-dependent as well as Sts5-independent mechanisms.
source: We also observed residual formation of Dcp1-mCherry dots, suggesting that Orb6 kinase can induce P-body formation via Sts5-dependent as well as Sts5-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: mRNA levels of ssp1, efc25 and psu1 declined upon Orb6 kinase inhibition.
source: We found that mRNA levels of ssp1, efc25 and psu1 declined upon Orb6 kinase inhibition (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Ssp1-HA protein levels decrease in orb6-as2 cells upon inhibition with 1-NA-PP1.
source: Consistent with the idea that Orb6 kinase prevents degradation and translational repression of Sts5-regulated mRNAs, immunoblotting analysis showed that Ssp1-HA protein levels decrease in orb6-as2 cells upon inhibition with 1-NA-PP1 (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6E and 6F.

claim: Normal Ssp1-HA protein levels were maintained in sts5∆ orb6-as2 cells upon inhibition of Orb6-as2 kinase.
source: Normal Ssp1-HA protein levels were maintained in sts5∆ orb6-as2 cells upon inhibition of Orb6-as2 kinase, in accordance with the findings that sts5 suppresses the viability phenotype of orb6 mutants and sts5Δ cells accumulate ssp1 mRNA.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6E and 6F.

claim: Ssp1-HA protein levels decline in temperature-sensitive orb6-25 cells cultured at the non-permissive temperature (36°C).
source: These observations held true also for Ssp1-HA protein levels in temperature-sensitive orb6-25 cells cultured at the non-permissive temperature (36°C) in the presence and absence of Sts5 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: Myc-Efc25 protein levels declined in orb6-as2 mutants grown in the presence of 1-NA-PP1.
source: Similarly to Ssp1-HA, Myc-Efc25 protein levels also declined in orb6-as2 mutants grown in the presence of 1-NA-PP1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), and sts5Δ abolished the reduction of Efc25 levels in orb6-as2 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: sts5Δ abolished the reduction of Efc25 levels in orb6-as2 mutants.
source: Similarly to Ssp1-HA, Myc-Efc25 protein levels also declined in orb6-as2 mutants grown in the presence of 1-NA-PP1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), and sts5Δ abolished the reduction of Efc25 levels in orb6-as2 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Cells over-expressing Orb6 kinase display significantly smaller Sts5- and Dcp1-containing particles than control cells, following growth for 1 hr in minimal medium without glucose.
source: Indeed, we found that cells over-expressing Orb6 kinase display significantly smaller Sts5- and Dcp1-containing particles than control cells, following growth for 1 hr in minimal medium without glucose (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: sts5∆ cells form significantly smaller and dimmer Dcp1-containing P bodies, as compared to control cells, following 1 hr growth in glucose deprivation conditions.
source: Further, consistent with Sts5 having a role in promoting, at least in part, P-body formation during nutritional stress we found that sts5∆ cells form significantly smaller and dimmer Dcp1-containing P bodies, as compared to control cells, following 1 hr growth in glucose deprivation conditions (shift from 2% to 0.01% glucose) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: Orb6 kinase prevents Sts5 recruitment to Dcp1-containing granules and attenuates P-body formation, in a manner that is at least in part Sts5-dependent.
source: Together, these findings support the idea that Orb6 kinase prevents Sts5 recruitment to Dcp1-containing granules and attenuates P-body formation, in a manner that is at least in part Sts5-dependent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The function of Orb6 kinase activity has the effect of decreasing the degradation of specific mRNAs.
source: Additionally, the function of Orb6 kinase activity has the effect of decreasing the degradation of specific mRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Orb6 kinase phosphorylates Sts5 in vitro.
source: We performed an in-vitro kinase assay by purification of Orb6 kinase regulatory subunit Mob2, as previously reported (Wiley et al., 2003; Das et al., 2009, 2015), using bacterially expressed Sts5. We found that the immunoprecipitate readily phosphorylates Sts5 (Figure 7A), suggesting that Orb6 kinase phosphorylates Sts5.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Sts5 contains several putative NDR kinase consensus sequences that are consistent with 14-3-3 binding sites when phosphorylated.
source: Sts5 contains several putative NDR kinase consensus sequences (Hao et al., 2008; Mazanka et al., 2008; Gógl et al., 2015) that are consistent with 14-3-3 binding sites (RxxS) when phosphorylated (Yaffe et al., 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: 14-3-3 protein Rad24 has a role in negatively regulating Orb6 substrate Cdc42 GEF Gef1.
source: We previously showed that 14-3-3 protein Rad24 has a role in negatively regulating another Orb6 substrate, Cdc42 GEF Gef1 (Das et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Sts5-HA physically associates with Rad24-GST and not with GST alone.
source: This assay confirmed that Sts5-HA physically associates with Rad24-GST and not with GST alone (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Sts5-3xGFP forms cytoplasmic puncta in rad24∆ mutants even when cultured in rich medium (YE) in the presence of glucose.
source: Consistent with Rad24 negatively regulating Sts5 recruitment, we found that Sts5-3xGFP forms cytoplasmic puncta in rad24∆ mutants even when cultured in rich medium (YE) in the presence of glucose (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: P-body formation is not strongly induced in either rad24∆ or control cells in growth conditions where cells are not starved.
source: This effect occurs in growth conditions where cells are not starved and P-body formation is not strongly induced in either rad24∆ or control cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: ssp1 mRNA levels do not significantly change in rad24∆ mutants as compared to control cells.
source: Accordingly, we found that ssp1 mRNA levels do not significantly change in rad24∆ mutants as compared to control cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Sts5-3xGFP association with GST-Rad24 is abrogated by inhibition of Orb6-as2 kinase activity following exposure of orb6-as2 cells to 1-NA-PP1.
source: We found that that Sts5-3xGFP association with GST-Rad24 is abrogated by inhibition of Orb6-as2 kinase activity following exposure of orb6-as2 cells to 1-NA-PP1, and not in orb6-as2 cells exposed to DMSO or in control orb6+ cells (Figure 7F; see quantification in Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sts5 protein associates with 14-3-3 protein Rad24 in a manner that is dependent on Orb6 kinase activity.
source: Collectively, our findings indicate that Sts5 protein associates with 14-3-3 protein Rad24 in a manner that is dependent on Orb6 kinase activity, and that this association prevents Sts5 coalescence into cytoplasmic puncta.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The association between Sts5 and Rad24 prevents Sts5 coalescence into cytoplasmic puncta.
source: Collectively, our findings indicate that Sts5 protein associates with 14-3-3 protein Rad24 in a manner that is dependent on Orb6 kinase activity, and that this association prevents Sts5 coalescence into cytoplasmic puncta.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Orb6 kinase localization is enriched at the growing cell tips during interphase.
source: Orb6 kinase localization is enriched at the growing cell tips during interphase, in a manner that depends on the pattern of growth of the cell (Figure 8A; Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,a,b,c and B) (Verde et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and a citation to previous work.

claim: In smaller cells, which grow in a monopolar manner, Orb6 kinase localization is higher at the old growing end and lower at the non-growing new end.
source: In smaller cells, which grow in a monopolar manner (M), Orb6 kinase localization is higher at the old growing end and lower at the non-growing new end (Figure 8A, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,a).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Most cells contain a few small Sts5 puncta during growth in rich medium.
source: As shown earlier (See Figure 2A), during growth in rich medium, Sts5 localization is generally diffuse. However, a closer inspection indicated that most cells contain a few small Sts5 puncta (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: There is an increase in the number and intensity of Sts5 puncta at the non-growing end of smaller cells.
source: We consistently found an increase in the number and intensity of Sts5 puncta at the non-growing end of smaller cells (Figure 8C; Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,d,e and f; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B), indicating an inverse correlation between Orb6 kinase localization at the growing tip and Sts5 aggregation (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is an inverse correlation between Orb6 kinase localization at the growing tip and Sts5 aggregation.
source: We consistently found an increase in the number and intensity of Sts5 puncta at the non-growing end of smaller cells (Figure 8C; Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,d,e and f; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B), indicating an inverse correlation between Orb6 kinase localization at the growing tip and Sts5 aggregation (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the microscopy data presented.

claim: In tea1∆ cells, Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into small puncta was clearly seen increasing towards the non-growing cell tip.
source: To further investigate this effect, we visualized Sts5-3xGFP in longer tea1∆ cells that grow from one end only (Snell and Nurse, 1994; Verde et al., 1995). tea1Δ cells display monopolar Orb6-GFP localization at the only growing cell tip (Figure 8D; Figure 8—figure supplement 2A,a). In these cells, Sts5-3xGFP recruitment into small puncta was clearly seen increasing towards the non-growing cell tip (Figure 8E-F; Figure 8—figure supplement 2A,b–f; Figure 8—figure supplement 2B: asterisk marks the growing tip).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8E-F and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Orb6 kinase activity negatively regulates Sts5 recruitment into cytoplasmic puncta, via interaction with 14-3-3 protein Rad24, in a manner that is spatially significant.
source: Collectively, our findings indicate that Orb6 kinase activity negatively regulates Sts5 recruitment into cytoplasmic puncta, via interaction with 14-3-3 protein Rad24, in a manner that is spatially significant: an asymmetry of Orb6 distribution between growing and non-growing tips correlates with an asymmetry in Sts5 recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: An asymmetry of Orb6 distribution between growing and non-growing tips correlates with an asymmetry in Sts5 recruitment.
source: Collectively, our findings indicate that Orb6 kinase activity negatively regulates Sts5 recruitment into cytoplasmic puncta, via interaction with 14-3-3 protein Rad24, in a manner that is spatially significant: an asymmetry of Orb6 distribution between growing and non-growing tips correlates with an asymmetry in Sts5 recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Orb6 kinase activity is repressed during mitosis by the septation-initiation network (SIN), which triggers cytokinesis.
source: Orb6 kinase activity is repressed during mitosis by the septation-initiation network (SIN), which triggers cytokinesis (Kanai et al., 2005; Gupta et al., 2013, Gupta et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: SIN signaling remains active until completion of cytokinesis, which is marked by closure of the contractile ring and a fully formed cell septum.
source: SIN signaling remains active until completion of cytokinesis, which is marked by closure of the contractile ring and a fully formed cell septum (García-Cortés and McCollum, 2009; Alcaide-Gavilán et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The derepression of MOR signaling, and of Orb6 activity, that results from inactivation of the SIN pathway promotes cell separation upon completion of cytokinesis.
source: The derepression of MOR signaling, and of Orb6 activity, that results from inactivation of the SIN pathway promotes cell separation upon completion of cytokinesis (Gupta et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Sts5-3xGFP puncta dissipate when the septum is fully closed and the actomyosin contractile ring protein Rlc1 disappears from the plane of cell division.
source: Consistent with Orb6 kinase re-activation, Sts5-3xGFP puncta dissipate when the septum is fully closed and the actomyosin contractile ring protein Rlc1, encoding myosin II regulatory light chain (Le Goff et al., 2000; Wu et al., 2006), disappears from the plane of cell division (Figure 8G,H; Wei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8G and 8H.

claim: Orb6 kinase inhibition maintains Sts5-3xGFP granules even following actin ring closure and Rlc1 disappearance.
source: Consistent with a role for Orb6 kinase reactivation in mediating Sts5-3xGFP granules dissipation, Orb6 kinase inhibition maintains Sts5-3xGFP granules even following actin ring closure and Rlc1 disappearance (Figure 8—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A and 3B.

claim: Microarray analysis found that Sts5 negatively regulates transcripts that encode cell wall proteins with potential functions in cell separation.
source: Supporting a role for Orb6 kinase and its substrate target Sts5 in cell separation, microarray analysis found that Sts5 negatively regulates transcripts that encode cell wall proteins with potential functions in cell separation.
evidence: This is supported by microarray data presented in Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Transcripts for a predicted β-1,3 glucanase (encoded by SPBP23A10.11C) and predicted β-glucosidase Psu2 are more abundant in sts5Δ cells.
source: Transcripts for a predicted β-1,3 glucanase (encoded by SPBP23A10.11C) and predicted β-glucosidase Psu2 are more abundant in sts5Δ cells (See Figure 3—source data 1), consistent with a role for β-1,3 glucan degradation in the primary septum during the process of cell separation (Martín-Cuadrado et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data and a citation to previous work.

claim: sts5Δ cells accumulate transcripts of the transcription factor Mbx1.
source: In addition, sts5Δ cells accumulate transcripts of the transcription factor Mbx1 (See Figure 3—source data 1) that cooperates with the transcription factor Ace2 to promote expression of endo-glucanase Agn1, a hydrolytic enzyme involved in septum degradation (Suárez et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data and a citation to previous work.

claim: Mbx1 cooperates with the transcription factor Ace2 to promote expression of endo-glucanase Agn1, a hydrolytic enzyme involved in septum degradation.
source: In addition, sts5Δ cells accumulate transcripts of the transcription factor Mbx1 (See Figure 3—source data 1) that cooperates with the transcription factor Ace2 to promote expression of endo-glucanase Agn1, a hydrolytic enzyme involved in septum degradation (Suárez et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Sts5 recruitment into puncta during mitosis, mediated by SIN pathway-dependent inhibition of Orb6 kinase, may function to translationally repress mRNAs encoding cell wall hydrolytic enzymes that would interfere with the deposition of the primary septum.
source: Thus, it is possible that Sts5 recruitment into puncta during mitosis, mediated by SIN pathway-dependent inhibition of Orb6 kinase, functions to translationally repress mRNAs encoding cell wall hydrolytic enzymes that would interfere with the deposition of the primary septum.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data presented.

claim: sts5∆ cells are prone to rupture at the site of cell separation.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that sts5∆ cells are prone to rupture at the site of cell separation (Figure 8—figure supplement 4A,d and B) similarly to cells that express ectopically active Orb6 during mitosis (Gupta et al., 2013, Gupta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 4A and 4B.

claim: Cells that express ectopically active Orb6 during mitosis are prone to rupture at the site of cell separation.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that sts5∆ cells are prone to rupture at the site of cell separation (Figure 8—figure supplement 4A,d and B) similarly to cells that express ectopically active Orb6 during mitosis (Gupta et al., 2013, Gupta et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: sts5Δ cell cultures display an increased percentage of cells growing in a bipolar fashion, as compared to similarly sized control cells, under exponential growth conditions.
